newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Wall St, French budget depress Euro stocks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Wall St, French budget depress Euro stocks.

text.p: A sharp fall on Wall Street depressed most leading European stock markets on Monday, with worries over the French state budget aggravating the woes of the Paris bourse.

But the German market leapt in early trading after news of a merger between Vereinsbank and Hypobank, although the euphoria quickly subsided and the market fell back as computer problems disrupted trade.

On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar/mark rate reacted little to a French audit of state finances which estimated that the public deficit would be 3.5-3.7 percent of gross domestic product this year.
This was well above the target for joining a single European currency but in line with market expectations.
Wall Street's profit-taking binge on Friday, which dragged the Dow Jones Industrial Average down 130.31 points to 7,890.46, was the main depressant for Europe.
But all financial markets wanted to know how the Socialist-led government in Paris would cut the deficit to qualify for economic and monetary union (EMU), and by how much.

Finance Minister Dominque Strauss-Kahn said he planned to cut the deficit by a further 0.4 percent. The prospect of higher company taxes to help achieve this weighed on prices. On the Paris bourse, the CAC-40 index was down 32.75 points (1.14 percent) at 2,843.94 by late morning.
The French factor was also felt indirectly in London as uncertainty over the scheduled 1999 launch for EMU has helped to strengthen sterling because Britain is unlikely to be a founding member.

Sterling's strength has hurt British exporters badly and depressed the stocks of a number of companies which rely heavily on foreign earnings. At mid morning the FTSE-100 index of blue chips was down 71.1 points or 1.46 percent at 4,806.1.
London dealers were also nervous about the Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Tuesday when Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan will report to Congress on the state of the U.S. economy.

Greenspan sent stock markets plunging around the world last December when he warned investors against irrational exuberance. Since then the bull run has resumed with a vengeance, pushing the Dow briefly through 8,000 points last week before the profit-takers cashed in.

But economists said there were few major clouds on the horizon for the U.S. economy. Since last year Greenspan has commented that he has no intention of trying to prick a stock market bubble with higher short-term interest rates.
Despite the profit-taking, London dealers said it was too early to say the bull run, which has pushed the FTSE up 20 percent this year, was over.

"At this stage I can't get too bearish," said the head of equity sales at one brokerage. "Not much has changed on the inflation and interest rate outlook...Any setback at the moment is going to be a short, sharp shock but not much more than that.
"The market may be a bit overvalued but some people were saying that six months ago and it hasn't done them much good," he said.

Frankfurt told a different story in early trade. The IBIS index of electronic trade jumped around 80 points to a high of 4,211.67 on news that two of Germany's largest commercial banks, Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypobank, would merge.

But the mood did not last and by late morning the IBIS fell into minus figures before recovering slightly. By late morning the IBIS was up 3.58 points at 4,135.52. The DAX index of floor trade was not quoted due to computer problems.
On the foreign exchanges the dollar edged higher to session highs above 1.79 marks and also crept up against the yen. Tokyo was closed on Monday for a public holiday.

The news from Paris, much of which had been leaked, had little effect. "Most of the damage has been done in anticipation of it. The government will have prepared the market for the worst," said Tim Fox, international economist at Standard Chartered.
The mark eased slightly to 3.3791 francs from 3.3805 late on Friday and a high of 3.3810 early on Monday.
CURRENCIES AT 0945 GMT
The dollar was at 115.90 yen and 1.7942 marks, compared with 115.35 yen and 1.7892 marks in late trading on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0945 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 71.1 points or 1.46 percent at 4,806.1.
FRANKFURT - The IBIS index of electronic trade was up 3.58 points at 4,135.52. The DAX index of floor trade was not quoted due to computer problems.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 32.75 points (1.14 percent) at 2,843.94.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 0945 GMT
Gold was fixed in the morning at $328.05 after closing at $324.15 an ounce on Friday. Silver was up one cent at $4.31.
